Being someone who loles to avoid large crowds, I would've liked to be one of them.
The view is outstanding. There are plenty of guides who will take you through and assist you all the way up and down for a price. Plenty of souvenir in shops at the end and even cafes serving food, beverages of all sorts including fresh squeezed juices.
I recommend this to anyone who can hike for 30 minutes up and steep inclines.

2000 years old complex spanning whole too if the mountain and spreading for hundreds of meters around the mountain.

This are quite picturesque

If you are in a rush and want  to only go up sunrise and down I think 1h is technically possible but I suggest allow 2h.

So the lesson here is if you visit during the Buddha birthday festival do a sunrise visit. Avoid daytime.

Sigiriya Rock: A Testament to a Dynasty’s Rise and Fall
This ancient city atop a giant rock, known as the “Sky Palace,” was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982. Built in the 5th century by King Kasyapa to escape his brother’s revenge, it took 18 years to complete. Abandoned after his reign, it was rediscovered by a British explorer in the 19th century.
1.Majestic Rock – A 200m-high landmark, best viewed from nearby cafes.
2.Architectural Wonder – A once-lion-shaped palace showcasing 1,500-year-old craftsmanship.
3.Cultural Treasures – Stunning frescoes and sculptures along the ascent.
4.Ancient Royal City – Features a moat, gardens, and a red-brick aerial fortress.
5.Breathtaking Views – Panoramic landscapes, especially at sunrise and sunset.
6.Tips – Wear light shoes, bring water, and protect against the sun.
